chapter: Recordings, later jobs and changing times
title: Larry's low register on the English records
summary: Russell asks about Larry's low-register solo on an English Columbia record; Harry admires his low tone and recalls hearing only that record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, I was wondering, to get back to that low register business, one of those English records, the original Dixieland made over there, had a solo by your brother all in the low register, which he didn't usually do in the other records. Yeah, I had that record. Did he ever play that way much around here? That is, did he keep going up and down covering the whole instrument or did he sometimes just stick to one register for a solo?

Well, I really don't remember, but Larry got a beautiful tone in the low register. Yeah. Now at that time, the equipment for recording, of course, you know what it was then. So his low register, I thought even though he played in the horn and the recording, you know, wasn't just, but his tone was really beautiful, I thought. Yeah. I'm forever blowing bubbles, you, you thinking of, huh?

I don't remember that, that's the title, it seems like another title to me too. I'm forever blowing bubbles. I don't have the record here now, it seems like some other tune that Joe Merez used later then too. A pop tune that he played that on.
Well, that was the only English recording that I heard. Did you use that low? That he played in the low register.
I think, this one just came out, but it must have been out in the old days too. Yeah. You have those old ones on Columbia, the 78s, or is that a long play that you have?
The Columbia? That's the English. Yeah, the English. Yeah, I had those, the 78s. Yeah, on 78, I never did get them on 78s.
I've still got a couple of them.
